title: Setup PCSX2 On Linux | PlayStation 2 Emulation on Linux | Desktop & Steam Deck
summary: Jov’s Gaming Lounge installs PCSX2 on Kubuntu through the portable AppImage route, making the same Linux package relevant to a desktop and Steam Deck while documenting the host hardware used for the demonstration.

blocks.text: The guide focuses on a Linux-specific deployment decision rather than repeating every graphics toggle. PCSX2 is obtained from the official download page, launched as an AppImage under KDE, and optionally integrated through AppImageLauncher. That route keeps the emulator package separate from a distribution repository and can transfer to SteamOS because the Deck also provides a Linux desktop environment. Listing the Ryzen 5 3600, Vega 56 and Ubuntu 20.04 test system gives the walkthrough a concrete host context instead of implying identical behavior everywhere.

The recording predates current PCSX2 packages and newer SteamOS releases, so AppImageLauncher compatibility, desktop permissions and file locations may differ now. An AppImage also does not update through every distribution’s normal package manager. Download only from the official PCSX2 domain, verify the executable permission and consult current project instructions before adding a third-party integration utility. The video establishes a workable Kubuntu-era installation path; controller mappings, legal firmware dumping, per-game settings and Gaming Mode shortcuts require separate validation on the target machine.
